claims.text: The as-cast or conventionally processed (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
The unchanged alloy exhibits a large caloric response.
The unchanged alloy has poor fracture toughness and load-bearing integrity.
The unchanged alloy tends to crack under operational loading.
Room-temperature severe plastic deformation followed by a short anneal near 600 °C can produce a bimodal grain structure in the target alloy.
The resulting heterogeneous structure will contain nano- or submicron grains dispersed within a coarse-grained matrix.
Ultrafine grains will impede crack initiation and propagation.
The ultrafine-grained portion of the heterogeneous structure will enhance ductility.
The ultrafine-grained portion of the heterogeneous structure will enhance fracture toughness.
Coarse grains will preserve the crystallographic environment required for the reversible phase transformation.
A reversible phase transformation is responsible for the target alloy's caloric effect.
The processed alloy will have significantly higher yield strength than the homogeneous control.
The processed alloy will have significantly higher fracture toughness than the homogeneous control.
The processed alloy will retain caloric entropy change comparable to the control under magnetic fields of about 2 T at 250–350 K.
The processed alloy will retain caloric entropy change comparable to the control under pressure cycling near 0.5 GPa at 250–350 K.
The proposed performance is applicable over 250–350 K, at about 2 T magnetic field and about 0.5 GPa pressure.
The integrity and caloric outcomes depend critically on annealing parameters that balance coarse-grain retention against ultrafine-grain formation.
The proposed benefit persists only within mechanical loading limits for which the bimodal microstructure remains stable.
